phase: Phase 8 — Existing Mechanism Manifestation Gap Audit

definitions.manifestation: The same mechanism realized through a meaningfully different operational process or decision structure.
definitions.parametric_variation: Different user, native object, amount, route, date, wording, or other parameter without a changed operational decision structure.
definitions.structural_variation: A changed transaction graph, mutation type, dependency type, precedence relation, or governed scope dimension.

manifestations.description: Two ordered one-way bookings compete for one one-shot certificate and one reusable gift card; the gift card can fund only the cheaper first booking, so the certificate must be preserved for the more expensive second booking.
decision_structure: plan two transactions before the first commit
recognize that any certificate use removes the certificate rather than preserving a residual balance
compare the gift card against both fares
allocate gift card to the first/smaller booking and certificate to the second/larger booking
variation_inside_manifestation: certificate face value and gift-card balance
manifestations.why_not_distinct_manifestations: All five preserve the same two-node transaction graph, the same resource applicability, the same cheap-first ordering, and the same opportunity-cost solution.

P4.main_gap: No admitted state changes the number/order of transactions, certificate applicability, fallback-resource structure, or allocation geometry.

manifestations.description: A general Business-cabin cancellation permission appears to authorize cancellation, but the more specific already-flown segment rule requires refusal or transfer.
decision_structure: observe an apparently qualifying Business reservation
apply the flown-segment exception before ordinary cancellation grounds
refuse or transfer rather than execute cancellation
variation_inside_manifestation: passenger count, membership, insurance, and payment history
manifestations.why_not_distinct_manifestations: Every state instantiates the same general-permission versus flown-lifecycle override and requests the same whole-reservation cancellation operation.

LGA01.main_gap: No admitted state exercises a different precedence relation, such as a different general eligibility rule, exception predicate, or operation-specific override.

upstream_manifestations.description: Cancel a pending gift-card-funded order and immediately restore its payment to the gift card.
Replace a pending order's whole-order payment method and refund the prior gift-card payment.
Change an item to a cheaper same-product variant and refund the price reduction to the gift card.

downstream_dependency_manifestations.description: Use the refreshed gift-card balance to replace another pending order's entire payment method.
Use the refreshed gift-card balance to pay the delta for an item upgrade in another pending order.

P3.main_gap: Downstream consumers remain limited to two types, and the upstream/downstream cross-product is sparse; all cases refresh the same gift-card balance resource.

manifestations.description: User authorization to substitute a destination does not expand the flight-modification operation's destination-preservation scope.
decision_structure: compare requested endpoint with the reservation's preserved destination
treat user authorization as insufficient to expand tool/policy scope
refuse or transfer instead of directly mutating the destination
variation_inside_manifestation: reservation, route, requested airport, and date
pure governance request versus P5 budget/choice composition
manifestations.composition_note: The P5×LGA04 state adds fare-search and budget reasoning, but its focal LGA04 boundary is still destination preservation; it is not a second scope manifestation.

LGA04.main_gap: No admitted state tests a different scope dimension such as passenger/object scope; composition changes surrounding reasoning but not the focal boundary.
